failure_reason: Genuine Home-scoped Bestsellers PLP found and confirmed, but its site-reported total (704) counts per-color-variant rows, not distinct products (documented site-wide quirk for quince.com, see notes/191.md), and only the first 30 rows are visible via any access tier - the widget's pagination cursor is ignored server-side by both the SSR page and the Next.js data route (verified identical row order/IDs on a cursor-advanced request), and the client-side loader hits a private api.onequince.com endpoint with no discoverable unauthenticated route. The true distinct-product count beyond the visible 30 rows cannot be verified exactly.
notes: Company is Quince (quince.com), a DTC brand spanning apparel and home; scoped strictly to the Home department per task instructions. Checked: homepage nav/mega-menu, /shop/home department page nav, embedded __NEXT_DATA__ nav tree (submenus for all departments), sitemap.xml -> sitemap_us.xml -> sitemap_shop.xml (full list of /shop/home/* URLs). Found genuine Home-scoped Bestsellers PLP at /shop/home/best-sellers (breadcrumb: home > best sellers; TITLE widget text 'Home Best Sellers'; FILTER_AND_SORT + PRODUCT_LIST widgets present with real product cards, colors/sizes/price filters). This is distinct from /shop/all/best-sellers (storewide, includes apparel/jewelry/beauty - out of scope per task instructions) and from per-department pages like /shop/women/best-sellers, /shop/men/best-sellers etc. found in nav but not relevant. No further genuine site-exposed sub-splits exist under Home Best Sellers (no 'Furniture Best Sellers'/'Lighting Best Sellers' nav children) - only one undifferentiated listing, so a single row is correct, not invented sub-categories. QTY: FILTER_AND_SORT widget reports total=704 and pagination.total=704, but per this exact site's documented count-inflation pattern (verified in a prior Home-Decor pass, notes/191.md: quince.com's own 'N items'/pagination.total counts one row per product-color variant, not one row per distinct product), the raw 704 cannot be taken as the distinct-product qty. Parsed the full PRODUCT_LIST widget JSON: among the 30 visible rows, only 25 distinct productId values appear (5 are color-variant duplicates of an already-seen product). pagination.hasMore=true (704 total rows exist server-side, only 30 delivered in SSR payload). Tried to retrieve further rows: (1) direct GET with cursor=n:30 on the same URL - server returned page 1 identically; (2) the Next.js data route /_next/data/34214719982/shop/home/best-sellers.json?cursor=n:30 - returned byte-identical widget data (same first-5 productIds: 450,331,273,1087,117) confirming the cursor is ignored server-side; (3) api.onequince.com (the client-side incremental-load target referenced in prior notes) has no discoverable public unauthenticated route. Per THE ONE RULE, qty is set to null rather than reporting the inflated 704 or an unverifiable estimate.

rows.evidence: FILTER_AND_SORT widget: {"total": 704} (color-variant row count, not distinct products - see notes); only 30 rows delivered server-side (pagination: {"cursor":"n:30","limit":30,"hasMore":true,"total":704}), of which 25 distinct productId values are visible (floor count)
rows.flag: MANUAL REVIEW: PAGINATION CEILING + COUNT-INFLATION - site's own total (704) is a per-color-variant count per this site's documented quirk, and only the first 30 of 704 rows are retrievable via any access tier tried (cursor/offset params ignored by both the SSR page and the Next.js data route; the client-side incremental loader targets a private api.onequince.com endpoint with no accessible unauthenticated route). Verified distinct-product floor from visible rows = 25. True distinct-product total for the full 704-row listing cannot be verified exactly.
